name: exult
why: A recreation of Ultima 7 engine is a fascinating look at how old games were engineered, though it needs game data files.

brief.what_it_is: Exult is an open-source engine that recreates Ultima VII (The Black Gate, with Serpent Isle as a sequel) for modern operating systems. It takes the original game's data, graphics, and plot files as input, which the user must supply from their own legal copy, and it outputs a playable game that runs natively on Windows, macOS, and Android. The project also ships Exult Studio, a level and content editor, and tools for the game's SHP graphics format.
brief.why_it_exists: The project's introduction says that as computers evolve, classic games risk being lost, and that Ultima VII, a two-part early-1990s RPG, still has a large following and is considered by many to be one of the most immersive games ever made. Exult aims to keep it running on modern systems.
brief.how_it_works: Exult is a reimplementation of the game engine that reads the original Ultima VII data, graphics, and music files rather than including them. The site's news says the engine was ported from SDL2 to SDL3 in its development tree, and that a 2026 release changed the Windows installer's helper DLL to be compiled with MSVC. The brew caveat notes that audio is configured in ~/Library/Preferences/exult.cfg, and that CoreAudio or an audio pack (use_oggs) can be selected there.
brief.install_notes: The Homebrew formula contains only the game engine, so you must supply your own legal copy of the Ultima VII game files for it to fully work. Audio is configured in ~/Library/Preferences/exult.cfg: set driver to CoreAudio for CoreAudio, and set use_oggs to yes to use the audio pack. The Windows installer can also download the audio packs and several mods. The homepage does not describe a first-run wizard.
brief.standout: Unlike a remake with new assets, Exult is a pure engine that depends on the original game files, and it has grown into a whole toolkit: an editor (Exult Studio), GIMP and Aseprite plug-ins for SHP files, an Android port, and a community Ultima VI remake mod that runs on the Exult engine.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage news runs to 27 March 2026 (Windows 1.12.1-1 re-release), 8 January 2026 (1.12.1 hotfix), and 11 May 2025 (1.12), with a development tree in progress. The project also notes that releases now come roughly every two years, with occasional hotfixes in between.
brief.caveats: You must provide your own legal copy of the Ultima VII game data, and the engine does not include it. Antivirus programs falsely flagged the Windows installer, which the project says was a gcc compile issue and has since been rebuilt with MSVC. The 2020 and 2022 news lists known issues, such as the antimagic rain from the cube generator not dissipating quickly enough and the game quitting rather than returning to the menu after the ending. Support for very old Windows versions (95, 98, ME, NT, 2000) ended with 1.6, and a legacy download exists for them. The homepage does not state a license.
quotes: Exult is a project to recreate Ultima VII for modern operating systems, using the game's original plot, data, and graphics files.
many consider it to be one of the most immersive games ever produced
Please play with it and tell us of any problem you encounter using the Github discussion page or bug tracker.

judge.reason: A maintained reimplementation of Ultima VII’s engine, with an editor and graphics-format tools, offers more to explore than simply replaying a classic game.

entry.title: Exult
entry.tldr: An open-source engine that runs Ultima VII, the early-1990s RPG, on modern systems by reading your own copy of the original game files.
entry.deeper_look:
Exult reimplements the Ultima VII game engine. It does not ship the game. You point it at the data, graphics, music and plot files from a legal copy of The Black Gate or its sequel Serpent Isle, and it runs them natively on current Windows, macOS and Android.

The project's stated reason is preservation: as computers change, classic games risk being lost. It describes Ultima VII as a game that "many consider to be one of the most immersive games ever produced". Keeping it playable means rebuilding the engine rather than emulating the old hardware around it.

That split between engine and data is the idea underneath. Because Exult has to read the original file formats, it has grown into a toolkit: Exult Studio, a level and content editor, plus GIMP and Aseprite plug-ins for the game's SHP graphics format. A community Ultima VI remake mod also runs on the engine. It is a good way to see how a game of that era was put together from data files and an engine that interprets them.
entry.install:
brew install exult
# The formula installs only the engine. You must supply your own legal copy of the Ultima VII game files.
# Audio settings live in ~/Library/Preferences/exult.cfg: set `driver` to `CoreAudio` for CoreAudio, and `use_oggs` to `yes` to use the audio pack.

try_this.what_happens: Lists the command-line options the engine accepts.
Starts the engine. With the original Ultima VII data in place, it loads the game.

entry.whats_unique: It is a pure engine with no bundled assets, rather than a remake with new art. It has also grown an editor, graphics plug-ins, an Android port and a mod ecosystem around it.
entry.caveats: It does nothing useful without your own legal copy of the Ultima VII data, and the project's news lists a few known issues, such as the game quitting instead of returning to the menu after the ending.
